talk.text: The doe bolts before you're close.
The reedcat bolts before you're close.
The buck bolts before you're close.

shy_terrace_doe.text: A terrace doe is grazing at the far side of the meadow, small and russet, with a white throat. It lifts its head.
One step closer and it will be gone into the terraces. It keeps going back to lick at a bare grey rock, where salt has dried in the cracks.

shy_terrace_doe.choose: Leave something out for it, and keep still?

do.text: You set the salt lick on a flat stone, back away downwind, and sit very still.
The doe comes, one careful step at a time. It eats. When it's done it looks at you for a long moment, and doesn't run.
When you get up to go, it follows.
You set the dried fish down and wait, downwind and still. The doe lifts its nose, and stays where it is. Whatever it wants, that isn't it.
You set the honey bread down and wait, downwind and still. The doe lifts its nose, and stays where it is. Whatever it wants, that isn't it.
You set the cave moss down and wait, downwind and still. The doe lifts its nose, and stays where it is. Whatever it wants, that isn't it.
You leave it be. The doe watches you until you're gone.

shy_fog_reedcat.text: Something grey moves at the edge of the cloud forest: a reedcat, so pale it's hard to see against the mist. Its eyes find you.
One step closer and it will be gone into the cloud. It's nosing at the bones of a trout someone cooked here and left.

shy_drove_buck.text: A drove buck stands on the rise, shaggy and heavy-horned, left behind by some herd. It stamps once.
One step closer and it will be gone into the hills. Where the drovers camp, it has licked the stones pale.
